title: a-seal-inside-a-seal-inherits
intention: A tester run started inside a tester sandbox inherits that sandbox's seals instead of building a second one: no bwrap is invoked inside a sandbox the tester built, the network seal and the instance seal are each read as INHERITED and still measured from inside, so a proof that drives cairn test as a subprocess runs green under the seal on a host whose AppArmor refuses nested namespaces.
why: Measured 2026-10-01: e038544a9b60's PROVED crossing refused with BuildGateRed on tester reds; three of them are nested-seal proofs refused by AppArmor unpriv_bwrap since linux 7.0.0-34 (kernel log: apparmor DENIED capable sys_admin profile unpriv_bwrap). Lived symptom: no tester ticket can reach PROVED.
traces_to: Law 9 and Law 7: a green proof that reds only because its sandbox cannot be built is a red for the wrong reason, and today it blocks every PROVED crossing in the tester component (BuildGateRed on e038544a9b60). The module's own rule (NetnsIsolation.wrap: 'ONE sandbox carrying both seals, never a sandbox inside a sandbox ... nesting would cost a second namespace whose failure modes nobody has measured') is now measured: the second namespace is refused outright.
how: In cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py: (1) a second marker INSTANCE_SEAL_MARKER = 'CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED', set with --setenv by instance_bind_flags so every sandbox carrying the instance swap says so, and inside_an_instance_seal() reading it; (2) both wrap() methods, when every seal they would add is already inherited (network marker for netns, instance marker for a swap), return ['env', '-C', cwd] + argv instead of a bwrap argv — one sandbox, never a sandbox inside a sandbox, which this module already says and which the host now enforces; (3) check_instance_seal gains the inherited branch the network seal already has: with the marker set it measures from inside that the instance root is a mount point in /proc/self/mountinfo and that a marker written there lands, and reads SEALED (inherited) only then — the marker without the mount reads BREACHED. In cairn/devices/tester/device.py the run skips snapshot_instance_space when the instance seal is inherited, so a nested run does not copy the outer swap. Proved by a new cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py.
falsifier: RED if: (1) inside an outer sandbox carrying both tester markers and an instance swap bound at the instance root, python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --netns over a directory holding one green fixture proof does not report it green; (2) a file the inner subject writes under the instance root is not in the outer swap afterwards, or appears in the live instance root; (3) check_instance_seal with the instance marker set but no mount at the instance root reads SEALED. Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because the three standing nested-seal proofs in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ are the receivers: they red at every reseal while a nested run cannot be sealed, and the build gate reads them at every PROVED crossing in the tester component
children: none, because the change is one marker, two wrap branches and one check branch in cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py plus one skipped snapshot in cairn/devices/tester/device.py
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) How does the proof get an outer sandbox when it is itself run plain? If inside_a_seal() and inside_an_instance_seal() are both true, the tester already built one around this proof, so the tooth runs the inner cli directly; otherwise the tooth builds the outer layer itself with bwrap --dev-bind / / --unshare-net --setenv CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED 1 --setenv CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED 1 --bind <scratch swap> ~/.cairn, which is not nested when the proof runs plain. Either way the cli runs one level inside a tester-shaped sandbox. (2) The fixture proof: a scratch dir somecomp/proofs/test_green_fixture.py printing one PASS line and exiting 0. (3) Clause 3 needs no sandbox: the mountinfo reader is a function over text, fed a mountinfo without the instance root. (4) PROVES = {ticket: {'1':..., '2':..., '3':...}}; resolve isolation names inside each tooth.
